articles.title: Bitcoin holds near $64,000 as a renewed Hormuz threat clouds US-Iran ceasefire talks
articles.snippet: Crypto firmed over the weekend after Friday's sell-off, with bitcoin recovering toward $64,000. Permanent ceasefire talks open in Switzerland, but Iran's order to close the Strait of Hormuz again revives the risk the deal was meant to settle.

articles.title: Schwab to join prediction markets race with S&P 500 event-based options: WSJ
articles.snippet: The planned offering would let customers bet on index moves as Coinbase and Robinhood expand in the sector.

articles.title: Digital credit market hit by huge selloff as Strive CEO blames leverage liquidations
articles.snippet: Matt Cole says forced selling from leveraged investors pushed STRC and SATA sharply lower before both rebounded.

articles.title: Live markets: Bitcoin under pressure as Saylor comments on STRC selloff
articles.snippet: About 20% of miners are now unprofitable, and publicly traded miners sold more than 32,000 bitcoin in the first quarter to cover operating costs, more than they offloaded in all of 2025.

articles.title: Bitcoin traders load up on bearish bets all the way down to $52,000
articles.snippet: Bitcoin traders are scrambling to buy options bets that would pay off if the selloff deepens.
